metadata.skill_name: ISO 8601 UTC Time Formatting and Parsing
metadata.objective: Perform standard ISO 8601 UTC time serialization and deserialization
metadata.section_summary: D3 is a collection of modules that are designed to work together; you can use the modules independently, or you can use them together as part of the default build.

skill_drafts.name: Time Format and Parse Operations
skill_drafts.description: Create and apply time formatters and parsers using strptime/strftime-inspired syntax for both locale-specific and UTC/ISO 8601 timestamps. Converts between time objects and formatted strings.
skill_drafts.objective: Convert between time objects and formatted strings using locale or standard conventions
applicable_signals: Need to format Date objects to human-readable strings
Need to parse time strings into Date objects
Working with UTC or ISO 8601 timestamps
Preparing time data for display or storage
contraindications: Performing timezone arithmetic or handling daylight saving time transitions
Working with relative time durations or time intervals
Handling complex temporal calculations beyond format/parse
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Select formatter/parser type', 'detail': 'Choose based on timestamp type: locale-specific, UTC, or ISO 8601'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Create formatter or parser', 'detail': 'Call appropriate function (format, parse, utcFormat, utcParse, isoFormat, isoParse) with format pattern if needed'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply to input', 'detail': 'Pass Date object to formatter or time string to parser'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Return result', 'detail': 'Formatted string or parsed Date object'}
triggers: Need to format Date objects to strings or parse time strings to Date objects; working with locale-specific or UTC timestamps
constraints: Format pattern must follow strptime/strftime conventions
Locale must be defined or use default locale
Input must be a valid Date object for formatting or valid time string for parsing
cautions: Ensure locale is properly initialized before using locale-specific formatters
ISO 8601 formatters/parsers assume UTC; do not use for timezone-aware conversions
Custom locale definitions must be set before use via timeFormatLocale or timeFormatDefaultLocale
output_contract: Returns a formatted time string (when formatting) or a parsed Date object (when parsing) that matches the specified locale and format pattern. Null or error if input is invalid.

examples.input: Date object: new Date(2024, 0, 15, 14, 30, 0); format pattern: '%Y-%m-%d'
Date object: new Date(2024, 0, 15); format: d3.utcFormat('%Y-%m-%d')

metadata.prompt: Use this skill to format Date objects into strings or parse time strings into Date objects. Choose the appropriate formatter/parser based on your locale and timestamp type: locale-specific (format/parse), UTC (utcFormat/utcParse), or ISO 8601 (isoFormat/isoParse). Apply the formatter or parser to your input and return the result.
metadata.section_summary: D3 is a collection of modules that are designed to work together; you can use the modules independently, or you can use them together as part of the default build.

skill_drafts.name: Locale-Specific Time Formatter Creation
skill_drafts.description: Define or retrieve a locale configuration and instantiate formatters and parsers bound to that locale's conventions. Enables repeated time formatting operations with consistent locale-specific rules.
skill_drafts.objective: Create a locale-bound formatter or parser object for repeated time formatting operations
applicable_signals: Need to format or parse multiple timestamps with the same locale
Switching between default and custom locale conventions
Preparing reusable formatter/parser functions for a session
contraindications: One-off time formatting where overhead of locale binding is not justified
Using only ISO 8601 or UTC standard formats without locale customization
Formatting timestamps that do not require locale-aware month or day names
intervention_moves: Call d3.timeFormatLocale(definition) to define a custom locale with locale-specific time names and formats
Call d3.timeFormatDefaultLocale(definition) to set the default locale globally
Retrieve the locale object and invoke .format(specifier), .parse(specifier), .utcFormat(specifier), or .utcParse(specifier) with a format string
Store the returned formatter/parser function for repeated use
triggers: Formatting or parsing multiple timestamps with the same locale; need to switch between default and custom locales
constraints: Locale definition must include required time format specifiers and locale-specific strings (e.g., month names, day names)
Format specifier string must follow strptime/strftime conventions
Locale object is immutable after creation; changes require creating a new locale
cautions: Custom locale definitions must be complete; missing specifiers will fall back to defaults or error
Setting the default locale affects all subsequent time formatting operations in the session
output_contract: Returns a locale object with bound methods (format, parse, utcFormat, utcParse) that accept a format specifier string and return a formatter or parser function ready for invocation on timestamp data.

examples.input: Create a formatter for a custom locale with French month names, then format a date
examples.output: const locale = d3.timeFormatLocale({...frenchMonthNames}); const fmt = locale.format('%d %B %Y'); fmt(new Date(2024, 0, 15)) → '15 janvier 2024'
examples.notes: Locale definition includes months, days, and format specifiers; formatter function is reusable

examples.input: Set default locale and use shorthand d3.timeFormat()
examples.notes: After setting default, d3.timeFormat() and d3.timeParse() use the new locale

metadata.prompt: To create a locale-bound formatter or parser: (1) Define or retrieve a locale configuration using d3.timeFormatLocale() for custom locales or d3.timeFormatDefaultLocale() to set the default. (2) Access the locale object's bound methods: format(), parse(), utcFormat(), and utcParse(). (3) Invoke the appropriate method with a format specifier string (e.g., '%Y-%m-%d') to obtain a formatter or parser function. (4) Reuse the returned function for multiple timestamp operations.
metadata.section_summary: D3 is a collection of modules that are designed to work together; you can use the modules independently, or you can use them together as part of the default build.

skill_drafts.name: ISO 8601 UTC Time Formatting and Parsing
skill_drafts.description: Format Date objects to ISO 8601 UTC strings or parse ISO 8601 UTC strings to Date objects. Provides standard UTC time serialization and deserialization without locale customization.
skill_drafts.objective: Perform standard ISO 8601 UTC time serialization and deserialization
applicable_signals: Need for interoperability with standard time formats
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Determine operation type', 'detail': 'Decide whether to format (Date → string) or parse (string → Date)'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Format operation', 'detail': 'Call d3.isoFormat(date) to convert Date object to ISO 8601 UTC string'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Parse operation', 'detail': 'Call d3.isoParse(string) to convert ISO 8601 UTC string to Date object'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Validate output', 'detail': 'Confirm string matches ISO 8601 format or Date object is valid'}
triggers: Storing times in canonical UTC format
constraints: Output is always UTC; no timezone offset customization
Input strings must be valid ISO 8601 UTC format
cautions: Ensure input Date objects are in UTC or convert before formatting
Parsed Date objects are in UTC; apply timezone conversion if local time is needed
output_contract: Returns either an ISO 8601 formatted UTC string (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:45Z) for format operations, or a valid Date object for parse operations. Both outputs are guaranteed to be in UTC.

examples.notes: Format operation: Date object to ISO 8601 string
Parse operation: ISO 8601 string to Date object

metadata.prompt: Use d3.isoFormat to convert a Date object to an ISO 8601 UTC string (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:45Z). Use d3.isoParse to convert an ISO 8601 UTC string back to a Date object. No locale configuration is required.
